ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the food web there are labels such as BLACK BEAR, BOBCAT, HAWK OWL, GRAY WOLF, MOOSE, CARIBOU, SQUIRREL, GRASS, EVERGREEN, BLACK SPRUCE. BLACK BEAR is located toward the upper middle of the figure, with multiple arrows around it pointing to BLACK BEAR, for example from the directions of BOBCAT, CARIBOU, MOOSE, GRAY WOLF, etc.; but no arrow starting from BLACK BEAR and pointing to other organisms is seen. Reasoning: In a food web, arrows usually indicate the direction of energy flow, that is, from food/prey to consumer/predator. If an organism has a predator, there should be an arrow from that organism to the organism that preys on it. In the figure, BLACK BEAR has no arrow leaving it and pointing to another predator, so it has no predator.
